name: Hoshaama
title: Descendant of King Jeconiah
summary: Hoshaama was a son of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah, who was taken into exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in the royal lineage of David in 1 Chronicles. As a member of the royal family in captivity, he represented hope for the continuation of David's dynasty.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the lineage of Jeconiah
keyEvents.description: Hosjama is listed as one of the sons of Jeconiah, the king of Judah who was taken into captivity in Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.

keyEvents.title: The Exile of Jeconiah to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Jeconiah, Hosjama's father, was taken captive to Babylon, marking the end of Judah's independent kingdom and the beginning of the exile.

keyEvents.title: The Royal Lineage in Exile
keyEvents.description: Despite the exile, David's lineage was preserved through Jeconiah's sons, including Hosjama, as a testament to God's promise to David.

keyEvents.title: Jeconiah's Restoration in Babylon
keyEvents.description: Jeconiah, Hosjama's father, was eventually released from prison in Babylon by King Evil-Merodach and given an honorable place at the king's table.
